replacement_html:
2.0 Structural Impossibility: A Disc Cannot Hold Its Own Shape

A 20,015-km-radius disc of Earth mass at Earth mean density requires ≈2.4 GPa of internal pressure to stand up against its own self-gravity — about twelve times the compressive strength of granite. The dome cannot invoke selective self-gravity as an out: the model's own Sun and Moon overhead are round, and roundness at large scale is the signature of self-gravity. If self-gravity rounds the Sun and Moon it also collapses the disc, in about fifteen minutes.

Why this argument goes first: Before we ask whether the dome's H(r) equation reproduces 7.83 Hz (§2.1), or whether its axial-symmetric field can generate the SAA (§2.10), we should ask whether the dome, as a physical object, can exist at all. If a self-gravitating Earth-mass body cannot maintain a disc shape, then every subsequent numerical dispute is downstream of a structural impossibility. This section shows that the dome's own commitments — Earth-mass, roughly Earth-mean density, and a round Sun/Moon overhead — are mutually inconsistent with a 20,000-km disc geometry.

The macro-physics kill-shot (no arithmetic required): Every large body in the observable universe is round. Roundness at scale is not a coincidence; it is the observable signature of self-gravity in hydrostatic equilibrium. The threshold radius above which self-gravity overcomes the yield strength of rock (the "potato radius") is only ≈200–300 km; Saturn's moon Mimas at 198 km radius is already round, Enceladus at 252 km is unambiguously so (Lineweaver & Norman 2010, "The Potato Radius"; Thomas 2010, Icarus). The dome's disc has a radius of 20,015 km — about 67× the potato-radius threshold. There is no known material configuration in which a rocky body sixty-seven times over the roundness threshold retains a non-spherical equilibrium shape. Every counter-example that would falsify this rule (a persistent large flat rocky body somewhere in the solar system) is absent from the observational record. The dome would be the sole exception to a rule with no known exceptions.

The disc-geometry arithmetic (corrected): The reviewer who prompted this section proposed the uniform-density sphere central-pressure formula Pc = 3GM²/(8πR⁴) as an analogy. That formula is derived for spherical geometry and does not apply directly to a disc; used with Earth's spherical radius it yields ≈170 GPa, but that number describes Earth, not the dome. The correct disc-geometry derivation goes: if the dome contains Earth's mass (5.972 × 10²⁴ kg) at Earth's mean density (5,515 kg/m³) and is a uniform disc of radius R = 20,015 km, the thickness is h = M/(ρ π R²) ≈ 860 km. For a self-gravitating uniform slab with R ≫ h, Gauss's law gives an internal gravitational acceleration linear in the distance from the midplane, and integrating dP/dz against that acceleration yields a central pressure Pc = (π/2) G ρ² h² ≈ 2.4 GPa. Granite's uniaxial compressive strength is ≈150–250 MPa (≈0.15–0.25 GPa; see e.g. Goodman 1989, Introduction to Rock Mechanics, ch. 3). The disc's central pressure exceeds granite's strength by a factor of ≈10–15. Rock cannot statically support this column; the material must flow.

The collapse timescale: Once material begins to flow — which it must, because the equilibrium pressure exceeds the yield stress — the shape rearranges on the free-fall timescale, tff = √(3π/32Gρ). At Earth mean density this is ≈895 seconds, or about fifteen minutes. Whatever configuration the disc started in, it does not persist geologically. The end state of a self-gravitating Earth-mass mass at Earth-mean density is uniquely determined by hydrostatic equilibrium: a sphere of radius ≈6,371 km. That is Earth as observed.

The internal-consistency dilemma (the tightest wedge): The dome model places a local Sun at 5,733 km altitude and a local Moon at 2,534 km altitude, both visibly round from any point beneath. The model does not claim they are illusions or projections; they are physical objects in the model's cosmology. But roundness at their scale (visible angular diameters of ≈0.5° at those altitudes imply physical diameters of tens to hundreds of kilometres, well above the potato-radius threshold) is itself the fingerprint of self-gravity. This produces an unavoidable dilemma:

  • If self-gravity operates on the Sun and Moon (as their roundness requires), then it also operates on the disc beneath — and the disc collapses. The model's own overhead objects testify against its ground plane.
  • If self-gravity does not operate, then the Sun and Moon have no physical reason to be round. The model must then supply an independent, non-gravitational, bespoke mechanism for the shape of every large body — one that rounds a Sun 5,733 km overhead but leaves the 20,015 km disc beneath perfectly flat. No such mechanism has been proposed.

The dome cannot have selective self-gravity that rounds the local Sun and Moon it places overhead while sparing the disc it stands on. This is not a numerical dispute about a coefficient; it is a categorical dead-end within the model's own commitments.

Anticipated escape hatches, closed:

  • "The disc is not Earth-density." Lowering density at fixed Earth-mass raises the disc's thickness proportionally (h ∝ 1/ρ), and the central pressure Pc ∝ ρ² h² ∝ M²/R⁴ — that is, the required central pressure is independent of density and depends only on the total mass and the disc radius. At Earth-mass and 20,015 km radius the central pressure is ≈2.4 GPa regardless of what fills the disc. The dome cannot lower this by picking a lighter material. And the roundness dilemma is unaffected: ice bodies above the potato radius are also round (Enceladus is ≈60% water ice).
  • "Self-gravity is disabled by the dome's aetheric physics." Then the Sun and Moon — objects the dome places physically overhead in this same physics — must be round for some other reason. No such reason has been offered, and the roundness of large bodies is a signature we observe universally in the solar system, including on bodies the dome model does not otherwise attempt to describe (Ganymede, Titan, Ceres, and Pluto are all much larger than the potato radius and all round). Disabling self-gravity to save the disc immediately falsifies the model's treatment of every large body it discusses.
  • "The disc is supported by aetheric or firmament tension from above." A support mechanism that redistributes 2.4 GPa of central pressure into an upward force must itself be capable of ≈2.4 GPa of tension without failing. Copper (the firmament material the dome specifies elsewhere) has a tensile yield of ≈70 MPa — smaller than the required tension by ≈35×. Any bespoke aetheric fluid required to bridge this gap is unfalsifiable and is not accompanied by an equation of state we can test.

Consequence: The dome fails the structural-existence test independently of every subsequent numerical dispute in this Part. Whether or not H(r) reproduces 7.83 Hz (§2.1), whether or not the axial-symmetric field generates the SAA (§2.10), whether or not V13 coordinates are circular (§2.9) — the object under discussion cannot hold its own shape long enough for any of those numerical disputes to be resolved. The dome is round physics wearing a flat costume, and the costume cannot bear its own weight.

Note on the rotating-firmament secondary argument (conditional): If the dome's "cast copper" firmament rotates once per sidereal day to produce the observed diurnal star motion, its rim speed at r = 20,015 km is v = 2π × 20,015 km / 86,164 s ≈ 1.46 km/s. Hoop stress in a rotating shell is σ = ρv² ≈ 8,960 × 1,459² ≈ 19 GPa. Copper's tensile yield strength is ≈70 MPa; the required hoop stress exceeds copper's yield by a factor of ≈270. This is a secondary and conditional argument — it applies only if the dome commits to a rigid rotating firmament (see §2.16 on the cast-copper firmament's closed loops). The primary self-gravity argument above stands unconditionally.

Cross-references: The Sun/Moon-roundness commitment referenced above is developed in §2.16 (cast-copper firmament) and in Part 3 (astrometry). The gravity magnitude assumed here (≈9.8 m/s² at disc surface) is the value the dome uses in §2.3 (gravity at the rim) and §2.8 (gravity gradient with latitude). The "no radial-only model can produce longitudinal structure" invariant developed in §2.10 is the analogue of this section's "no flat rocky body at 67× the potato radius can persist" invariant — both are geometry-only kill-shots that no parameter refinement can escape.

prose_patches.note: Insert the new <details id="2-0-structural-impossibility"> block immediately before the existing §2.1 anchor. No renumbering of §2.1..§2.16 required — the new section is 2.0.

prose_patches.new: Guide for skimmers: §2.0 (structural impossibility) is the argument that runs BEFORE any of the numerical disputes below — it asks whether the dome can exist as a physical object at all, and shows that its own commitments to a round Sun/Moon overhead force self-gravity to also collapse the disc beneath. §2.9
prose_patches.note: Add §2.0 as the first-among-strongest in the skimmers guide. Preserves the existing §2.9 and §2.1 mentions that follow.

holes_addressed: Part 2 currently has NO macro-physics precursor to the numerical self-contradiction sections; every argument targets a specific dome equation or reference value. If a reader accepts that all sixteen §2.x-labeled contradictions can be defended one at a time, they never encounter the higher-order question 'can this object exist at all?'

The dome's own commitments to a round local Sun and Moon are used elsewhere in the review (§2.16 cast-copper firmament, Part 3 astrometry) but the internal-consistency wedge — that any large body's roundness is itself the signature of self-gravity — has not been made explicit as an argument against a flat disc.

The reviewer's proposed disc central-pressure figure (~170 GPa) is the uniform-density SPHERE formula applied to Earth's radius, not the dome's. Publishing that number would be a correctness liability — this EXP derives the correct disc-geometry pressure (≈2.4 GPa) and the correct rock-strength ratio (≈12×) so the number can survive scrutiny.
new_evidence_added: Lineweaver & Norman 2010, 'The Potato Radius: A Lower Minimum Size for Dwarf Planets', arXiv:1004.1091 — roundness threshold ~200–300 km for rocky bodies.
Thomas 2010, Icarus 208 — figures of Saturnian satellites confirming that Mimas (198 km) is already round.
Goodman 1989, Introduction to Rock Mechanics — granite compressive strength ~150–250 MPa (used as the ceiling on non-hydrostatic stress that rock can hold statically).
Standard result for the central pressure of a self-gravitating uniform slab: P_c = (π/2) G ρ² h². Derived in the section from Gauss's law + dP/dz = ρ g(z).
Standard free-fall timescale t_ff = √(3π/32Gρ) at Earth mean density → ≈895 s ≈ 15 min.

arithmetic_derivation_notes.reviewer_proposed_figure: ~170 GPa via P = 3GM^2/(8πR^4) with R = Earth's spherical radius 6371 km
arithmetic_derivation_notes.reviewer_proposed_figure_verdict: not applicable — the sphere formula uses Earth's spherical radius, not the disc's geometry. That number describes Earth, not the dome. Using the same formula with R = 20,015 km yields ~1.7 GPa (still ~8× rock strength) but is dimensionally the wrong derivation.

correct_disc_derivation.step_1: Impose Earth-mass at Earth-mean-density: V = M/rho = 5.972e24 / 5515 = 1.083e21 m^3
correct_disc_derivation.step_2: Impose disc radius R = 20,015 km: A = pi R^2 = 1.259e15 m^2
correct_disc_derivation.step_3: Solve for disc thickness: h = V/A ~ 8.60e5 m ~ 860 km
correct_disc_derivation.step_4: Self-gravity of uniform slab (R >> h regime), Gauss's law: g(z) = 4 pi G rho |z| toward midplane
correct_disc_derivation.step_5: Hydrostatic equilibrium: dP/dz = rho g(z); integrate from surface z=h/2 (P=0) to midplane z=0
correct_disc_derivation.step_6: Central pressure: P_c = (pi/2) G rho^2 h^2 ~ 2.36 GPa
correct_disc_derivation.step_7: Compare to granite compressive strength ~200 MPa: P_c / P_rock ~ 12x

arithmetic_derivation_notes.density_independence_note: At fixed Earth-mass and disc-radius, P_c = (pi/2) G rho^2 h^2 where h = M/(rho pi R^2), so P_c = M^2/(2 pi R^4) — independent of density. Result: ~2.4 GPa regardless of what material fills the disc.
caveats: The slab formula P_c = (pi/2) G rho^2 h^2 assumes horizontal extent R >> h (here R/h ~ 23, so the approximation is reasonable but not exact); a full 3-D self-gravitating disc calculation would yield a modestly different coefficient but the same order of magnitude.

The 200 MPa granite figure is a compressive-strength ceiling; the mantle already flows plastically at ~100-500 MPa on geological timescales, so 'rock cannot hold this pressure statically' is a stronger claim than 'rock breaks at this pressure'. Either framing supports the qualitative kill-shot.
The roundness threshold varies with material (rock ~ 300 km, water ice ~ 200 km). The disc at 20,015 km is ~67-100x threshold either way.

anticipated_objections.objection: The disc's density is not Earth-mean density — it could be much lower.
anticipated_objections.response: At fixed Earth-mass and disc-radius, lowering density raises the disc's thickness proportionally (h ∝ 1/ρ), and the central pressure P_c = (π/2)Gρ²h² = M²/(2πR⁴) — independent of density. Result: ≈2.4 GPa regardless of what fills the disc. The dome cannot escape this by choosing a lighter material. And the roundness dilemma is untouched: ice bodies above the potato radius are also round.

anticipated_objections.objection: Self-gravity might be disabled or modified by the dome's aetheric physics.
anticipated_objections.response: Then the model must explain why the local Sun and Moon overhead are round. Roundness at scale IS the observable signature of self-gravity in hydrostatic equilibrium. Disabling self-gravity to spare the disc simultaneously falsifies the model's ability to explain why every large body it discusses is spherical.

anticipated_objections.objection: The disc might be supported from above by firmament tension.
anticipated_objections.response: A tension mechanism that redistributes 2.4 GPa of central pressure into an upward force must itself sustain ≈2.4 GPa of tension without failure. Copper (the firmament material the dome specifies elsewhere) yields at ≈70 MPa — smaller by ≈35×. Any bespoke aetheric-fluid rescue is unfalsifiable and unaccompanied by an equation of state.

anticipated_objections.objection: The reviewer originally cited ~170 GPa as the required pressure and you have used 2.4 GPa — did you weaken the argument?
anticipated_objections.response: The 170 GPa figure was the reviewer's uniform-density SPHERE formula applied to Earth's radius, which describes Earth (which is spherical), not the dome. The correct disc-geometry derivation is 2.4 GPa. The qualitative kill-shot is unchanged: rock cannot statically support 2.4 GPa; it is still ≈12× granite's compressive strength; the disc still collapses on the same 15-minute timescale. Publishing a defensible number (2.4 GPa, correctly derived) rather than a headline-friendly but incorrect one (170 GPa) is what preserves the argument's survivability under adversarial review.

anticipated_objections.objection: Selective self-gravity is not impossible in principle — you could postulate that self-gravity operates on 'natural' bodies (Sun, Moon) but not on the 'constructed' dome disc.
anticipated_objections.response: This concedes the entire scientific project: the dome would no longer be a rocky body governed by physics, but a designed artifact governed by unspecified selection rules. The dome model does not currently claim this (it derives the disc's gravity from the same G that operates on other masses). Introducing a case-by-case selection rule to save the disc is a bespoke rescue that removes the model from the falsifiable-physics category entirely.

kernel_of_truth: The dome is right that a flat-Earth-shaped body of the disc's dimensions requires an internally consistent physical account. It correctly recognizes that gravity, if operating conventionally, would collapse the disc. Its response — invoking an aetheric or firmament-mediated support mechanism — is at least honest about the problem. The kernel: the dome recognizes that a flat rocky Earth needs a non-trivial physics story. The failure: the story it tells is inconsistent with its OWN other commitments (round local Sun and Moon, cast-copper firmament with specific material properties). The dome cannot simultaneously (a) commit to a round Sun and Moon overhead, (b) commit to Earth-mass with surface g ≈ 9.8 m/s², and (c) commit to a disc geometry, without also committing to a self-support mechanism that violates the material properties of every candidate material.

tldr_section_summary: A 20,015-km-radius disc of Earth mass at Earth mean density requires ≈2.4 GPa of internal pressure to stand up against its own self-gravity — about twelve times the compressive strength of granite. The dome cannot invoke selective self-gravity as an out: the model's own Sun and Moon overhead are round, and roundness at large scale IS the signature of self-gravity. If self-gravity rounds the Sun and Moon it also collapses the disc, in about fifteen minutes.
placement_rationale: Reviewer explicitly recommended top-of-Part-2 placement. Structurally justified: this argument makes every subsequent numerical dispute in Part 2 conditional on a prior structural claim. If a reader is convinced the object cannot hold its shape, the H(r) / SAA / V13 disputes become 'given the object cannot exist, does its stated equation nonetheless reproduce X' — which is a weaker frame than 'the object we're discussing can exist AND still fails these numerical tests'. Leading with §2.0 forces the model into the harder position first.
newsworthy: The dome cannot hold its own shape: correctly-derived arithmetic shows any Earth-mass disc at 20,000 km radius needs ≈12× granite's strength to resist self-gravity — and the model's own round Sun and Moon overhead prove self-gravity is real in this universe.
